title: Old Testament Survey II: Poetry and Prophets
summary: Job to Malachi: the Bible's books of wisdom and worship, and the messages of the prophets.
description: This course surveys the poetic and wisdom books (Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and Song of Solomon) and the prophets from Isaiah to Malachi. It explains each book's setting, main message and key passages, and shows how the prophets called God's people to repentance and pointed forward to the Messiah and the new covenant.
objectives: Introduce the wisdom and poetic books and how to read them
Explain the role and message of the Old Testament prophets
Place each prophet in Israel's history
Show the prophets' witness to Christ and the new covenant
outcomes: Summarise the message of Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and Song of Solomon
Explain what a prophet was and did
Place the major and minor prophets before, during or after the exile
Explain key messianic prophecies such as Isaiah 53 and Micah 5:2
Explain the promise of the new covenant in Jeremiah 31

modules.title: Job and Psalms
modules.intro: Job wrestles with suffering; the Psalms give words for every season of the soul.

lessons.title: Job: suffering and the sovereignty of God
lessons.body:
Job was "perfect and upright" (Job 1:1), yet he lost wealth, children and health. Heaven's scene shows that Satan accused him and God permitted the trial (Job 1-2).

Job's three friends insisted he must have sinned. Job protested his innocence and longed for God to answer, yet declared, "I know that my redeemer liveth" (Job 19:25).

When God spoke from the whirlwind, He did not explain the reasons but revealed His wisdom and power in creation (Job 38-41). Job humbled himself, and God restored him. Suffering is not always punishment; God is wise even when we cannot see why.

lessons.title: The Psalms: Israel's hymnbook
lessons.body:
The 150 psalms were Israel's songs and prayers, many by David. They are arranged in five books (1-41, 42-72, 73-89, 90-106, 107-150).

There are psalms of **praise** (Psalm 100), **lament** (Psalm 13), **thanksgiving** (Psalm 30), **wisdom** (Psalm 1), **repentance** (Psalm 51) and **trust** (Psalm 23).

The Psalms teach us to bring every feeling to God honestly, and to move from complaint to trust. Calvin called the book "an anatomy of all the parts of the soul".

lessons.title: Christ in the Psalms
lessons.body:
Jesus said the psalms spoke of Him (Luke 24:44). Some psalms speak of the anointed King, David's greater Son.

- Psalm 2: God's Son set as King over the nations (Acts 13:33).
- Psalm 16: the Holy One would not see corruption, fulfilled in the resurrection (Acts 2:25-31).
- Psalm 22: "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?", the cry from the cross (Matthew 27:46), with piercing of hands and feet (Psalm 22:16).
- Psalm 110: Christ seated at God's right hand, a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek (Hebrews 5:6).

terms.def: Books such as Job, Proverbs and Ecclesiastes that teach how to live in God's world.
A prayer of complaint or sorrow brought honestly to God.
A psalm that speaks of the coming Messiah, fulfilled in Christ.
One who buys back or rescues; Job's hope in God.
A word in the Psalms probably calling for a pause.
God's supreme rule and authority over all things.

texts.teaches: Job knew his Redeemer lives.
Seeing God, Job humbled himself and repented.
Ask God to create a clean heart.
The cry of forsakenness that Christ uttered on the cross.
The LORD tells David's Lord to sit at His right hand.

summary: Job teaches that suffering is not always punishment and that God is wise and sovereign.
The Psalms give words for praise, lament, repentance and trust.
Many psalms point to Christ: His kingship, death, resurrection and priesthood.
Bring every feeling to God honestly, moving from complaint to trust.

questions.q: What did Job's friends wrongly insist?
options: That he must have sinned to suffer so

questions.q: How did God answer Job from the whirlwind?
options: By revealing His wisdom and power in creation

questions.q: Which psalm contains the cry Jesus uttered on the cross?
How many psalms are in the book of Psalms?

modules.title: Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and Song of Solomon
modules.intro: Three books of wisdom: skill for daily life, the search for meaning, and the gift of married love.

lessons.title: Proverbs: wisdom for daily life
lessons.body:
Proverbs, mostly from Solomon, teaches skill in godly living. Its theme verse: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction" (Proverbs 1:7).

It speaks to speech, work, money, friendship, anger, sexual purity and family. It contrasts two ways: wisdom and folly, the righteous and the wicked.

Proverbs are general truths, not promises for every case. For example, "A soft answer turneth away wrath" (Proverbs 15:1) is usually true, but not always. Christ is the perfect Wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:24).

lessons.title: Ecclesiastes: life under the sun
lessons.body:
The Preacher (traditionally Solomon) explores pleasure, work, wisdom and wealth "under the sun", that is, life viewed without God. His verdict: "vanity of vanities; all is vanity" (Ecclesiastes 1:2), meaning everything is fleeting like vapour.

Yet he also sees that life is God's gift to be enjoyed with gratitude (Ecclesiastes 3:12-13), that God "hath set the world in their heart" (3:11), and that God will bring every work into judgement.

His conclusion: "Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man" (Ecclesiastes 12:13).

lessons.title: Song of Solomon: married love
lessons.body:
The Song of Solomon is a love poem celebrating the joy, longing and faithfulness of love between a bride and bridegroom. It honours God's gift of romantic and physical love within marriage, and warns not to awaken love before its time (Song of Solomon 2:7).

Its conclusion: "love is strong as death... Many waters cannot quench love" (Song of Solomon 8:6-7).

Many Christians through history have also seen in it a picture of Christ's love for His church (compare Ephesians 5:25-32). Its first meaning, however, is a celebration of pure married love.

terms.def: A short, memorable saying expressing a general truth about life.
In Proverbs, a person who rejects God's wisdom and instruction.
In Ecclesiastes, something fleeting and empty, like vapour.
Ecclesiastes' phrase for life viewed from a merely earthly point of view.
To fear God and keep His commandments (Ecclesiastes 12:13).
God's perfect knowledge and skill, personified in Christ.

texts.teaches: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart and He will direct your paths.
Life without God is vanity of vanities.
Fear God and keep His commandments: this is the whole duty of man.
Many waters cannot quench love.

summary: Proverbs teaches practical godly wisdom; its proverbs are general truths.
Ecclesiastes shows the emptiness of life without God and calls us to fear Him.
Song of Solomon celebrates pure love within marriage.
Christ is the perfect Wisdom of God.

questions.q: What is the theme verse of Proverbs?
What does "vanity" mean in Ecclesiastes?
options: Something fleeting and empty, like vapour

questions.q: What is the conclusion of Ecclesiastes?
options: Fear God and keep His commandments
Work is the meaning of life

questions.q: The first meaning of Song of Solomon is:
options: A celebration of pure married love

modules.title: Isaiah and Jeremiah
modules.intro: Two great prophets: Isaiah, the evangelical prophet, and Jeremiah, the weeping prophet.

lessons.title: What is a prophet?
lessons.body:
A prophet was God's spokesman, sent with "Thus saith the LORD". Prophets mostly **forth-told**, calling people back to the covenant, warning of judgement and promising mercy to the repentant. Sometimes they **foretold** future events.

True prophets were tested: their words had to agree with God's law and come to pass (Deuteronomy 13:1-5; 18:22).

The prophetic books are often grouped as **major** (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel, Daniel) and **minor** (the twelve shorter books). "Minor" refers to length, not importance.

lessons.title: Isaiah: holiness and salvation
lessons.body:
Isaiah ministered in Judah about 740 to 690 BC. He saw the Lord "high and lifted up" and heard "Holy, holy, holy" (Isaiah 6:1-8).

He warned of judgement, yet gave the clearest Old Testament pictures of the Messiah: born of a virgin, Immanuel (Isaiah 7:14); "unto us a child is born" (9:6); the suffering Servant "wounded for our transgressions" (53:5).

Chapters 40-66 comfort the people with promises of return from exile and of new heavens and a new earth (Isaiah 65:17). Isaiah is quoted in the New Testament more than almost any other prophet.

lessons.title: Jeremiah and Lamentations
lessons.body:
Jeremiah prophesied from about 627 BC until the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BC. Called as a youth, he was told, "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee" (Jeremiah 1:5). He faced rejection, beatings and prison for warning that Judah would fall to Babylon.

Yet he promised a **new covenant**: God would write His law on their hearts and remember their sin no more (Jeremiah 31:31-34), fulfilled in Christ (Hebrews 8:8-12).

**Lamentations** mourns Jerusalem's ruin, but in the middle confesses, "his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness" (Lamentations 3:22-23).

terms.def: A person sent by God to speak His word to His people.
Proclaiming God's word to the present situation, calling for repentance.
Predicting future events by God's revelation.
The longer prophetic books: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Ezekiel and Daniel.
Isaiah's figure who suffers for the sins of others, fulfilled in Christ.
God's promise to write His law on hearts and forgive sin fully, fulfilled in Christ.

texts.teaches: A word that does not come to pass was not spoken by the LORD.
The seraphim cry that the LORD of hosts is holy, holy, holy.
A virgin shall conceive and bear a son called Immanuel.
The Servant was wounded for our transgressions.
God will put His law in their inward parts and write it in their hearts.

summary: Prophets spoke God's word: calling to repentance and sometimes predicting the future.
Isaiah reveals God's holiness and the coming Messiah, the suffering Servant.
Jeremiah warned of Babylon and promised the new covenant.
Lamentations mourns judgement yet trusts God's faithfulness.

questions.q: Why are some prophets called "minor"?
Which chapter of Isaiah describes the suffering Servant wounded for our transgressions?
Which passage promises the new covenant?
Which book contains "great is thy faithfulness"?

modules.title: Ezekiel and Daniel
modules.intro: Two prophets in exile in Babylon: Ezekiel the priest-prophet and Daniel the statesman-prophet.

lessons.title: Ezekiel: the glory departs and returns
lessons.body:
Ezekiel was taken to Babylon in 597 BC and prophesied there to the exiles. He saw God's glory in a dramatic vision (Ezekiel 1) and later saw that glory leave the defiled temple (Ezekiel 10).

He taught personal responsibility: "The soul that sinneth, it shall die" (Ezekiel 18:20), and God's desire that the wicked turn and live (18:23).

After Jerusalem fell, he brought hope: a new heart and a new spirit (36:26), dry bones brought to life (37), and a vision of a renewed temple to which the glory returns (43:4-5).

lessons.title: Daniel: faithful in Babylon
lessons.body:
Daniel was taken to Babylon as a youth in 605 BC. He "purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself" (Daniel 1:8). God gave him wisdom to interpret Nebuchadnezzar's dreams.

His friends would not bow to the golden image and were delivered from the fiery furnace (Daniel 3). Daniel kept praying though it meant the lions' den (Daniel 6).

The lesson: God rules over the kingdoms of men (Daniel 4:17), and His people can live faithfully in a hostile culture.

lessons.title: Daniel's visions of the kingdoms
lessons.body:
Daniel 2 and 7 describe four world empires, commonly understood as Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece and Rome, followed by God's kingdom, a stone "cut out without hands" that fills the earth (Daniel 2:44-45).

In Daniel 7, "one like the Son of man" receives an everlasting kingdom from the Ancient of days (7:13-14). Jesus took this title for Himself (Mark 14:62).

Daniel 9 speaks of seventy weeks and the Messiah being "cut off" (9:26). Christians differ on the details of the later visions; all agree they show God's sovereign plan ending in the triumph of His kingdom.

terms.def: The visible display of God's presence and majesty.
Ezekiel's role: to warn the people of coming judgement.
Ezekiel's vision of God bringing His people back to life.
In Daniel 7, the heavenly figure who receives an everlasting kingdom; Jesus' favourite title for Himself.
Daniel's title for God the eternal Judge.
Daniel 9's prophecy of a period leading to the coming of the Messiah.

texts.teaches: The soul that sins shall die; each person is responsible.
God promises a new heart and a new spirit.
Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself.
The Most High rules in the kingdom of men.
The Son of man receives an everlasting dominion.

summary: Ezekiel saw God's glory leave the temple and promised a new heart and restoration.
Daniel lived faithfully in Babylon and God delivered him and his friends.
Daniel's visions show God's kingdom triumphing over world empires.
Jesus is the Son of man who receives the everlasting kingdom.

questions.q: Where did Ezekiel prophesy?
What does Ezekiel 36:26 promise?
options: A new heart and a new spirit

questions.q: Who were delivered from the fiery furnace?
Which title from Daniel 7 did Jesus apply to Himself?

modules.title: The Twelve: Hosea to Malachi
modules.intro: The twelve minor prophets span three centuries, from before the exile to the last word of the Old Testament.

lessons.title: Prophets before the exile
lessons.body:
**Hosea** married an unfaithful wife as a picture of God's faithful love for unfaithful Israel. **Joel** warned of the day of the LORD and promised the outpouring of the Spirit (Joel 2:28), fulfilled at Pentecost. **Amos** cried for justice: "let judgment run down as waters" (Amos 5:24). **Jonah** was sent to Nineveh and learned God's mercy to the nations. **Micah** foretold the Messiah's birth in Bethlehem (Micah 5:2) and summed up true religion: to do justly, love mercy and walk humbly with God (6:8).

**Obadiah**, **Nahum**, **Habakkuk** and **Zephaniah** speak of judgement on the nations and on Judah, yet "the just shall live by his faith" (Habakkuk 2:4).

lessons.title: Prophets after the exile
lessons.body:
**Haggai** urged the returned exiles to finish the temple: "Consider your ways" (Haggai 1:5). **Zechariah** encouraged them with visions and messianic prophecy: the King coming "lowly, and riding upon an ass" (Zechariah 9:9), and the one "whom they have pierced" (12:10).

**Malachi**, about 430 BC, rebuked careless worship, broken marriages and robbing God in tithes (Malachi 1-3). He promised the Lord would suddenly come to His temple, preceded by a messenger (3:1), and that Elijah would come before the great day (4:5), fulfilled in John the Baptist (Matthew 11:14).

lessons.title: Four hundred silent years
lessons.body:
After Malachi there were about four hundred years without a new prophet. During this time Persia gave way to Greece under Alexander, then to the Romans. The synagogue spread, and the Hebrew Scriptures were translated into Greek (the Septuagint).

God was preparing the world: one common language, Roman roads, and a people longing for the Messiah. "When the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son" (Galatians 4:4).

The Old Testament ends with a promise and an expectation; the New Testament opens with the coming of the One promised.

terms.def: The twelve shorter prophetic books from Hosea to Malachi.
The time when God acts decisively in judgement and salvation.
Doing what is right, especially toward the poor and oppressed.
The roughly four hundred years between Malachi and the New Testament.
The Greek translation of the Old Testament made before Christ.
Malachi's promised forerunner, fulfilled in John the Baptist.

texts.teaches: God will pour out His Spirit upon all flesh.
Let judgment run down as waters and righteousness as a mighty stream.
God requires us to do justly, love mercy and walk humbly with Him.
The King comes lowly, riding upon an ass.
God will send Elijah before the great day of the LORD.

summary: The twelve minor prophets span before, during and after the exile.
They called for repentance, justice and faithful worship.
They foretold the Spirit's outpouring, the Messiah's birthplace and His humble entry.
After Malachi, four centuries of silence prepared the world for Christ.

short.q: What is the main lesson of the book of Job?
short.model: Suffering is not always punishment for sin; God is sovereign and wise even when we do not understand, and we should trust Him.

short.q: Name two kinds of psalms and give an example of each.
short.model: For example, a lament such as Psalm 13 and a psalm of praise such as Psalm 100.
They spoke God's word to His people, calling them back to the covenant, warning of judgement and promising mercy, and sometimes foretold future events.

short.q: How does Isaiah 53 point to Christ?
short.model: It describes the Servant wounded and bruised for our transgressions, bearing the sins of others, which Christ fulfilled on the cross.

assignments.title: A psalm for life
assignments.prompt: Choose one psalm of lament (for example Psalm 13, 42 or 77). Explain its movement from complaint to trust, verse by verse, and describe how it could help a believer going through a hard time today.

assignments.title: Christ in the prophets
assignments.prompt: Choose three messianic prophecies from this course. For each, give the KJV reference, explain it in its original setting, and show where and how the New Testament says it was fulfilled.
